items.t: Bill Gates says getting countries to agree on AI regulations will be harder than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations
items.d: The Microsoft co-founder said he believes governments should be involved in monitoring what AI does and that it won’t slow down the industry’s progress.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Bill Gates says getting countries to agree on AI regulations will be harder than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations The Microsoft co-founder said he believes governments should be involved in monitoring what AI does and that it won’t slow down the industry’s progress. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Add to Google Bill Gates says it’s ‘not enough to have a kill switch’ for AI: Full interview 31:56 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 27, 2026, 9:00 AM EDT / Updated Sept. 27, 2026, 10:10 AM EDT By Alexandra Marquez Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates called on the U.S. to be a leader in regulating the growth of artificial intelligence but warned that getting countries to agree on a global framework could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era negotiations to limit nuclear weapons. “This is more difficult than that was,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Wednesday during a wide-ranging discussion on AI that aired Sunday. His remarks came as he spoke about President Donald Trump’s stance against regulating AI. The president earlier this month rejected calls for the federal government to impose guardrails for companies building AI models, saying in a post on Truth Social , “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.” Gates argued Wednesday that regulating AI companies by imposing monitoring systems would not hamper the U.S. in any race with China to develop superior technology. “What he said is fine, but I think after he hears from me and other people, including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is, that, you know, we will come to a consensus,” the tech mogul said. AI 기사요약 트러스톤자산운용이 신안 풍력 발전소를 인수하며 국내 재무적투자자 최초로 20MW 규모의 풍력 발전소 리파워링 사업을 추진한다. 국내 FI가 주도하는 풍력 발전 리파워링 첫 사례 트러스톤 누적 투자 규모 445MW… 수익률 20% 넘어 발전 사업 책임지는 '개발형 투자'… 에너지 전문가도 적극 영입 재생에너지 투자 선구자로 불리는 트러스톤자산운용이 운용하는 펀드가 전남광주 신안에 3메가와트(MW) 규모 풍력 발전소를 인수했다. 트러스톤은 2030년 이 발전소의 발전 용량을 20MW 수준으로 확대하는 리파워링도 추진하기로 했다. 국내 재무적투자자(FI)가 주도하는 첫 번째 풍력 발전소 리파워링 사례가 될 전망이다. 27일 투자은행(IB) 업계에 따르면 '트러스톤 ESG 신재생 펀드 2호'는 최근 동국S&C로부터 신안풍력발전 지분 100%를 인수했다. 신안풍력발전은 전남광주 신안에 3MW 규모 풍력 발전소를 운영하는 법인이다. 여기서 생산한 전력은 직접 전력구매계약(PPA)을 맺은 SK이노베이션 E&S에 판매된다. 전력을 최종 소비하는 건 넥센타이어 양산공장이다. 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임은 사용자에게 있습니다. 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 박종관 기자 기사댓글 개의 댓글이 있습니다. 댓글 닫기

items.t: Some lawmakers doubt a Congress that’s ‘barely capable of email’ can regulate AI
items.d: WASHINGTON — Amid warnings that artificial intelligence could soon wipe out humanity, some lawmakers are not confident that Congress has the expertise or ability to regulate AI.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Some lawmakers doubt a Congress that’s ‘barely capable of email’ can regulate AI Congress’ slow pace and inexperience with AI are colliding with a fast-moving technology. Though one Democrat countered: “We don’t have to be biologists or chemists to set up the FDA.” Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 NBC News; Getty Images Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 26, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT By Scott Wong WASHINGTON — Amid warnings that artificial intelligence could soon wipe out humanity , some lawmakers are not confident that Congress has the expertise or ability to regulate AI. “A lot of them can’t spell it,” quipped Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C. “They just don’t have the experience.” Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., was equally skeptical. “They still don’t know how to get on the internet,” let alone understand AI, he said. Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., who represents parts of Silicon Valley, argued that many members of Congress are just not up to speed on AI, and some seem uninterested. “The problem in Congress is not that we don’t have enough computer scientists. It’s that we don’t have enough people who have a basic understanding of how the technology works or are using it,” Khanna said in an interview with NBC News. Add to Google Rogue OpenAI model hacks Australian government website 01:53 “It’s like talking about making the rules for driving the road. Capitol Hill has been notoriously slow to regulate new technology. items.t: Meta opens early access program for new Muse features
items.d: Anyone interested in joining has to ask Muse to put them on the list.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 1:34 PM PDT · September 25, 2026 Image Credits: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto (opens in a new window) / Getty Images Sarah Perez Meta opens early access program for new Muse features After announcing a host of new features for Meta’s Muse AI app at its Connect 2026 developer conference this week, the company is opening up requests for early access. Meta shared on Friday that you can now ask Muse to put you on the list to try out its latest capabilities before anyone else. Meta posted a link to a prompt on X that, when shared with Muse, will log that you’re interested in joining Meta’s early access program. Just announced lots of new features…want early access? Your Muse can ask for you. Click below to drop a prompt into Muse👇 https://t.co/wI5YXmz50b — Muse (@Muse) September 25, 2026 (If you don’t want to click through, you can just copy and paste the prompt: “Can you let the Muse team know I want to be part of the Muse early access program?”) While typically companies offer pilot tests or betas with select users, they often A/B test with a randomized group to gain feedback and measure results. In this case, however, Meta is looking for AI enthusiasts to try its features first. That tactic could help it stay ahead of the competition, given that this crowd tends to use multiple AI apps and agents and has a good understanding of the market. As to what the new features will be? Meta teased many of those at Connect, including the launch of a digital avatar for Muse that you’ll be able to video chat with, tons more shopping partnerships and connectors, and an expansion of the Muse Mac app, which will soon be able to use your computer to complete various tasks. The company also said that Muse would be coming to Meta’s lineup of AI glasses , so users can interact with the agent just by speaking a wake word, then issuing a command. items.t: Mark Wahlberg is coming to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, and he wants to talk about your work, not his
items.d: Mark Wahlberg joins Bruce K. Lee at Disrupt to discuss investing, entrepreneurship, healthcare, wellness, and building businesses.
items.fullText: Let’s just get this out of the way: Mark Wahlberg is as A-list as it gets. He broke out in 1997’s “Boogie Nights,” and in the nearly three decades since, he’s built one of the highest-wattage careers in Hollywood: two Academy Award nominations, a Golden Globe nod for “The Fighter,” multiple Emmy nominations as a producer (HBO’s “Entourage” among them), and a filmography that spans crime dramas, comedies, and action blockbusters. Right now, he’s back on-screen in “By Any Means,” a manhunt thriller set during the 1966 Mississippi civil rights killings. He’s also signaling where he’s increasingly turning his attention. Wahlberg will sit down with Bruce K. Lee , founder and CEO of Keebeck Wealth Management , on the main stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to talk about that progression. Grab your ticket here so you don’t miss a moment of this session and Disrupt 2026. Ticket prices increase when the clock strikes 11:59 p.m. PT tonight. Image Credits: TechCrunch From Hollywood to business venture His acting career is really just part of the picture. Over the past two decades, Wahlberg has built a production company, a restaurant chain, apparel and fitness ventures, a slate of angel investments, and the now-25-year-old Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation, which supports inner-city kids and teens. He’s used his Hollywood success to launch big projects well outside the movie business — and in a fireside chat at this year’s Disrupt, he’s going to give us a peek into how. items.t: Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved
items.d: Bill Gates called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved in monitoring The Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist said AI is capable of helping bad actors harm billions of people. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Add to Google Bill Gates says AI 'powerful enough' to cause 'a billion deaths' 01:18 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 25, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT By Alexandra Marquez Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates on Wednesday called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress. “No one thinks self-regulation is enough,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in an interview set to air in full Sunday. Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether there needs to be legislation passed in Washington, Gates said, “Absolutely.” “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” he said. “And that has to be a required thing. And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.” Earlier this month, the CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the nation’s biggest AI labs, agreed that the race to develop powerful AI systems should slow down . Their statements on the issue came after a whistleblower who recently resigned from Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, publicly declared that “neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon added in a series of social media posts and interviews that week. items.fullText: 판타지의 경계를 확장하다: 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지가 도쿄게임쇼 2026에서 펼치는 캐릭터 IP와 리테일의 미래 2026/09/23 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 9월 17일부터 20일까지 일본 지바현 마쿠하리 멧세(Makuhari Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 있다. 관람객 다니엘 아세로(Daniel Acero) 씨는 “처음 봤을 때 스크린 화면인 줄 전혀 몰랐고, 투명한 설치물이라고 생각했다”면서 “마치 화면 뒤에 실제 공간이 있는 것처럼 깊이감이 느껴져서 놀라웠고, 이러한 방식으로 게임 캐릭터를 소개하면 게임에 대한 관심을 높이고 캐릭터의 개성을 효과적으로 전달할 수 있을 것”이라고 말했다. 관람객 동선과 대기 공간에는 32형 스페이셜 사이니지가 설치돼 부스 전반으로 캐릭터 경험을 확장했다. 32형 제품은 49.4mm의 얇은 두께로 좁은 공간에도 유연하게 설치가 가능해, 게임 체험을 기다리는 관람객을 대상으로 캐릭터와 세계관에 대한 몰입도를 유지했다. 관람객 토마스 포르티에(Tomas Portier) 씨는 “대기 줄이 길었지만, 스페이셜 사이니지 화면을 items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning, using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. items.fullText: University of Manchester Uses NVIDIA Earth-2 to Forecast Air Pollution Across the UK Manchester physicists David Topping and Hao Zhang applied NVIDIA Earth-2 generative models to air quality forecasting — unlocking predictions fast enough to inform public health. September 15, 2026 by Isha Salian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. items.fullText: ‘Now We Can Know Everything and Do Anything,’ Jensen Huang Says at Dreamforce At Dreamforce, Salesforce and NVIDIA announced Koa, a CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, post-trained from Nemotron on 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence — and running entirely within Salesforce’s own infrastructure. September 15, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Know everything. Do anything. That was the message NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang brought to Salesforce Dreamforce Tuesday, joining CEO Marc Benioff onstage in an appearance that coincided with the announcement of Koa — Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang didn’t just take the stage. He walked into the crowd — threading through the audience at Moscone Center, mic in hand, with Benioff alongside. “We’re all following you, bro,” Benioff told Huang at one point, drawing applause. “With electricity, we could power everything,” Huang said, tracing the arc of industrial revolutions. “With the internet, you can find anything. And now, with artificial intelligence as an infrastructure layer across the planet, we can know everything and do anything.” That arc led directly to the announcement. Salesforce’s first reasoning model was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on a proprietary synthetic dataset drawn from nearly three decades of enterprise CRM deployments. AI Safety When Benioff asked Huang about AI safety, Huang was direct. “Safety is paramount in a lot of ways. It’s job one,” Huang said. “However, safety is an engineering problem.
